To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the average download time of a peer is proportional to the number of other peers in the network, that the variance of the download time is proportional to the square of the number of peers in the network and that the average download rate of a peer is inversely proportional to the number peers in the network.
• In the case of P2P systems, the file dissemination time is proportional to log N for a large enough number of peers N, where N is the number of peers.

1) the performance of P2P file dissemination systems can be improved significantly by allowing users with different upload capacities to participate in the system, 2) the performance of the P2P systems can be further improved by allowing users to download linear combinations of file pieces rather than individual pieces, and 3) the performance of network coding systems is very sensitive to the number of users in the system and the number of file pieces.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the most efficient P2P system is the one which maximizes the number of downloads per unit time.

, for P2P networks with a single source and a large number of users, the optimal scheme for disseminating a file is to divide the file into M parts and then have each user download one of the M parts from a random peer.
the most efficient way to distribute a file is to use a P2P network and that network coding is the most efficient way of distributing a file in a P2P setting.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the file dissemination process in P2P systems can be modelled using the classical theory of queuing networks, and that this approach can be used to derive the performance metrics of the system.
the performance of the system depends on the number of parts M, the number of users N, and the distribution of upload capacities of the users.
we study the effect of upload capacity on the performance of the system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of the file dissemination scheme depends critically on the distribution of upload capacities amongst the users in the system.
the file dissemination time can be reduced if users with a high upload capacity are given preference.
a network coding based scheme is more effective in terms of reducing the download delay for users with high upload capacities than a scheme that does not use network coding.
